headline: After a breezy, seasonable Saturday and a quiet Sunday around New York City, a fast-moving storm brings a soaking 0.75 to 1 inch of rain and gusty winds late Sunday night into Monday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Saturday stays dry and breezy with seasonable temperatures across the city and surrounding area, caught between low pressure departing to the north and high pressure to the south, with gusts of 25 to 30 mph. Plenty of clouds hang around, especially in the morning into early afternoon. Winds ease late tonight.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Sunday is dry. A storm tracking up from the southern Plains passes to the north Monday, dragging a cold front through with a period of moderate rain late Sunday night into Monday morning, a widespread 0.75 to 1 inch falling over 6 to 12 hours, though no flooding concerns are expected. A narrow line of heavier showers may cross Long Island and Connecticut Monday morning; lightning isn't expected, but it could bring brief heavier rain and stronger gusts. South winds gust to about 25 to 35 mph late Sunday night, then west winds gust to about 30 to 40 mph Monday, with a chance of reaching Wind Advisory levels, most likely Monday afternoon behind the front; winds gradually subside Monday night.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Tuesday and Wednesday look dry and quiet behind the storm. The discussion does not go into detail beyond midweek.

coast: The Gale Warning for local waters has been canceled; Small Craft Advisories remain in effect for all waters today, easing tonight as winds lighten (ending this evening for some waters and between 1 and 6 AM Sunday for others). Gales are possible again Sunday night through Monday night with the frontal system: south gusts up to 40 knots (about 45 mph) late Sunday night into Monday morning, and gusts up to 40 knots continuing Monday as winds shift to the west and northwest.
watch_for: Rain timing and amounts late Sunday night into Monday morning
Possible Wind Advisory-level gusts Monday, especially Monday afternoon
A narrow line of heavier rain and stronger gusts Monday morning on Long Island and in Connecticut
confidence: Forecasters are confident in a breezy, dry Saturday and quiet Sunday, and fairly confident in a quick-hitting rain Sunday night into Monday, with less certainty about how strong Monday's winds get.
